text.p: Retailer Coles Myer Ltd said on Tuesday that its performance was running above expectations in the first quarter of 1996/97.
"First quarter performance is running above expectations," chairman Nobby Clark told the annual meeting in response to a question.
Clark did not quantify the first quarter result.
He said Coles was seeing something of a rejuvenation in its businesses, which range from department stores, discount operations, and retail grocery outlets.
"We are on the edge of something pretty good," he said.
Earlier, Clark told shareholders that the Melbourne-based retailer saw an improved bottom line peformance in 1996/97 as long as it had a reasonable Christmas period.
This turnaround was due to the impact of internal changes which were undertaken in the previous financial year.
"We hope it can continue," Clark said of the first quarter performance.

Coles Myer, Australia's largest department store operator and one of the two largest grocery retailers, suffered a sharp downturn in 1995/96 net profit to A$280.4 million from A$423.4 million a year earlier.
